cells.remarks: Records the gift of certain taxes by the king for offerings and worship to the God and same privileges to the residents of the streets called Vīrarājēndra-tirumaḍaivilāgam around the temple. Signed by a Chōlakulamānikka-Mūvēnda-vēlaṇ. The privileges granted to the residents were the sounding of drums on all occasions, auspicious and otherwise, for the śrīnudras and śrimāhēśvaras, and gongs in case of other residents. They were allowed to build storeyed buildings with lime-plaster and to enjoy generally all other concessions granted to the tirumaḍaivilāgam of the Āluḍaiyār temple.

cells.reference: ARE, 1915, no. 96-A; Ibid, part II, para 19
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxx||18" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXX, No. 18</button>
cells.remarks: Registers that some special privileges of honour (variśaigal) were conferred on certain Abhimānaśōlā Bhatṭaṇ and the temple servants including tapasyas, dēva-radiyār, and drummers living within the tirumaḍaivilāgam of the temple by the king. It is stated that they were allowed to hoist (the flag?) Rājādhirājaṇ, to ride (on?) a horse and to sound drums (bhēri) and gongs (śekaṇdigai) evidently when going out in procession. In addition to the above, they were allowed to have a second floor for their houses, two entrances is front, and the privileges of covering their house with plaster.

cells.remarks: Records gift of the village of Teṇkarai Niyamam alias Virarājēndra-nallūr in Vađapariśāra-nāđu, for worship, charity, and repairs, to the shrine of Tirukkāma-kōṭta-Nāchchiyār in the same temple, for the merit of Āṇdakkaṇ. The trustees of the temple (dēvarkanmi) were required to take up the managements of the village. All the taxes (irai puravu) such as chirrāyam, elavi, ukavai, maṇrupāđu, tendakurram, vēndukōl, eruttirai, sumai-suṇkam, śārikai and others being thus granted to the temple and the king ordered that the sāmantas must not enquire into the working of the trustees, but leave them to audit the accounts themselves.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Samastabhuvanaikavīra, etc. of the inscription of the Vikrama Pāṇdya III = (c. 1283.96). Records the construction of streets round the temple from the income of which worship had to be performed to the image of the Goddess Teṇnavaṇ-Mādēviyār set up in the temple. The king Vīra-Pāṇdya is given the birudas, 'the result of the meritorious deeds of the Lunar race', 'the Lord of Mathurāpuri', 'the gloom of the Karṇātakas' 'a lion to the elephant Gandagōpala', 'the Lord of Kāṇchipura', 'a garuḍa to the serpent Gaṇapati', etc.

Records the gift of a day's allowance (pađi) per year from their allotment by the members of the bodies (said to be members of an establishment tandiram, probably military in character) such as nađuviraśa-makkattār, ammaṇaṅgakāran, sēnāpatigal, nāyakañjeyvār, etc., for providing food offerings to god Ālūđaiyār Idaṅgaināyaka-Īśvaramuda1. The protection of the ārūsamakkaṭtār was invoked for the gift.

Note: 1. This name of the god suggests that the above said bodies belonged to the Iđaṅgai class and the deity was set up for worship by the members of the class.

The taxes and dues freed were otṭachchu, arāṭchi, elavai, ugavai, kāṇikkai, vāśalviniyā [o] am, vēṇdukōl, manđalamudalamaippēru, mudal, eljuttu-viniyōgam, kadamai, and antarāyam. cells.findspot: On the north wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: The praśasti describes that the king wielded his sceptre righteously held up his silver-white parasol, made the lands of the country fertile, gave relief to the suffering inhabitants, received only his one-sixth share (of the produce of the land), removed sins and seated on the royal throne afforded protection to his subjects from external evils and was as tenderly attached to them as the mother to the child she had given birth. The object of the inscription is to register a gift of 55 kalaṇju of gold as weight by Parakēsaari-kal each coin bearing clear marks and having proper weight made by Vīrasangādan Sūrriyadēvaṇ Vāṇavaṇ-Uttaramantri, a Nānādēśiya-nāittu-cheṭti of Nadiyanallūr in Vaṭakarai-Tirukkaĵumala-nādu. The quantity of gold was received by the members of the sabhā of Vīrasangāda-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Teṇkarai-nādu who bound themselves to meet from the annual income of 110 kalam of paddy for kār and pāśānam, arisisng from the deposited amout (1) the expenses of 90 kalam of paddy per year for feeding daily three brāhmaṇas at the rate of three kuruṇi calculated at one kuruṇi each, (2) 18 kalam and nine kuruṇi of paddy per year, at the rate of five nāli by the parakesari measure per day, for the man who cooked the meals; and (3) one kalam and three kuruṇi for cloth to the latter.

cells.reference: ARE, 1908, no. 304; Ibid, part ii, para. 26, 81
cells.remarks: Records provision for the maintenance and supervision of an irrigation channel, anicut and tank at Sūralūr alias Sundara-Pāndya-nallūr in Vāyaraikka-nādu, which belonged to the temple of Kurakkuttali-Āludaiya-Nāyanār. The villagers and the temple trustees stipulated that, in consideration of certain income and privileges granted to him, the fisherman Pillaiyān of Veļlaur in Pērū-nādu had to look after the said anicut (aṇai) and the channel, had to see that the water did not escape above the dam but was properly directed into the tank, notice the defects, if any, in the tank and the dam and report the matter to the villagers and the temple authorities and that on this information the village servant (veṭṭiyā) had to repair the dam, receiving as remuneration for that duty a piece of rent-free land and some payments in grain. Pillaiyān was also to collect the taxes vāyakkālpāttam (canal tax) pāśippāttam (fishing tax) from the temple tenants as Sūralūr.

cells.reference: ARE, 1905, no. 578; SITI, iii, part i, no. 1092, 1064-61
cells.remarks: States that the maṇdapa and prākāra of the temple of god Tirunāgēśvarasvāmin at Vijayamaṅgalam were reconstructed and that before beginning the work of renovation copies of all the inscriptions registering the gift of twilight lamps found on the walls were made and re-copied after the work was completed of such copies made the following are found: 1) Record dated in the 14th year in the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōladēva registering the gift of one puduchchalāgai achchu of gold by one of the captains, vellālaṇ-padaittalai, properly stationed at Vijayamaṅgalam. 2) Another record of the same year, i.e., the 14th regnal year of Kulōttunga-Chōla registering a similar gift by kaikkōlar. 3) Record dated in the second year in the reign of Vīrarājēndradēva registering the gift of one puduchchalāgai achchu by a captain vēlālaṇ-padaittalai. 4) Another record dated in the 2+1st year in the reign of Vīrarājēndradēva registering a similar transaction by a paṭṭāli-veṭtuvan of Vijayamaṅgalam. The record stops with this.3 Note: 1. Summary from SITI2. S. 1085 (SITI)3. From the Epigraphical Report it is learnt that one more transaction, the 5th, of the reign of Vīrarājendra is also found engraved there.

text.remarks:
States that the maṇdapa and prākāra of the temple of god Tirunāgēśvarasvāmin at Vijayamaṅgalam were reconstructed and that before beginning the work of renovation copies of all the inscriptions registering the gift of twilight lamps found on the walls were made and re-copied after the work was completed of such copies made the following are found: 1) Record dated in the 14th year in the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōladēva registering the gift of one puduchchalāgai achchu of gold by one of the captains, vellālaṇ-padaittalai, properly stationed at Vijayamaṅgalam. 2) Another record of the same year, i.e., the 14th regnal year of Kulōttunga-Chōla registering a similar gift by kaikkōlar. 3) Record dated in the second year in the reign of Vīrarājēndradēva registering the gift of one puduchchalāgai achchu by a captain vēlālaṇ-padaittalai. 4) Another record dated in the 2+1st year in the reign of Vīrarājēndradēva registering a similar transaction by a paṭṭāli-veṭtuvan of Vijayamaṅgalam. The record stops with this.3

Note: 1. Summary from SITI2. S. 1085 (SITI)3. From the Epigraphical Report it is learnt that one more transaction, the 5th, of the reign of Vīrarājendra is also found engraved there.

cells.remarks: Registers an order of the assembly of the village of Ottanūr alias Perumpalāṇam in Vaṇapariśāra-nādu. The tank at Avaraippallam in the eastern portion of the village which had been lying in a damaged condition for a long time was repaired providing bund and sluices at the expense of certain private individuals and the village assembly assigned the lands irrigated by the said tank to several persons who contributed for the expense of repairs, stipulating that they were to enjoy the full produce for the first four years and then give vāram probably to the assembly at the rate of 1/4th for the next three years, subsequently raising the rate of 1/3 and finally one-half.

cells.remarks: Records gift of the village Iraṭṭai-yaṇpāđi in Vaigāvi-nāđu for renovation to a number of temples situated in Karaivali-nāđu. Refers to an invasion of the king in which Karaivali-nadu was devastated and damage done to the temples located in it and states that the above gift was granted as an expiatory measure. Mentions that the temples (1) Vīra-Chōlīśvaram-Uḍaiyār, (2) Adirādirādichchurm-uḍaiyār1 and the temple of the goddess attached to it, (3) Vīrarājēndra-Iśvaramuḍaiyār (4) Rājarāja-Iśvaramuḍaiyār, and (5) Tirumaruđudaiyār of Kadarrūr were devastated due to the invasion. Note: 1 Perhaps king Adhirājarāja apparently lent his name to this temple. Kongu itself was known as Adirājarāja-maṇdalam, perhaps, after his king in the time of Chola sovereigns Vīrarājēndra and Rājēndra.

cells.remarks: Defines the four boundaries of the tirumađaivilāgam (i.e., 'the sacred premises of the temple' (?) and records an order of the king Kōnēriņmaikonđa (1) that an enquiry, if required, was to be instituted by the temple trustees only, as to which of the people living within the premises had not till then paid the taxes called daṇđakkurām and maṇrupādu, (2) that these collections when made from the defaulters, were to be presented to the temple treasury (3) that the king's officers should not enter into the temple premises defined above in order to make collections; (4) that the assessments, cess etc., payable to the royal treasury were to be pardoned: and (5) that the property of residents who were servants of the temple was to be confiscated to the temple treasury after their death, if they left no issue.

cells.remarks: Records gift of land for offerings to the ten Ālyārs in the temple of Alagar at Tirumāliruṇjōlai1 in Kīl-Iraṇiyamutṭta-nāđu,2 a s.d. of Pāṇdi-manḍalam. The land was situated in the village of Ulaguđaiyapirāṭti-chaturvēdimaṅgalam3 in Rājarāja-valanāđu which was split up from Karaivali-nāđu. Also provides for a festival in the temple called Vīrarājēndran-śandi, named after the Vīrarājēndra. Note: 1. This temple which was situated in Tirumāliraṇ-jōlai is mentioned in the Vaishnava hymns known as Nālāvira-prabandham. It may be noted that Teṇ-(southern) Tirumāliruṇjōlai is the name of Sevilipēri in the Tinnevelly district.2. This Kīl-Iraṇiyamutṭta-nāđu, i.e. the estern Iraṇiyamutṭtam, was the district from which hailed the Tamil poet Peruṅgan-singaṇṇār.3. This suggests that the queen after whom it was so called was designated Ulguđaiyapirāṭti. But, it is not improbable that this was a queen of Vīrarājēndradēva who, in ARE, 1909, no. 192, is called Ulaguđai-Perumāl.

cells.remarks: Records that when Arimitaiya-Māvali-Vāṇarāyar was ruling over Gaṅga-nāđu, Puṛamalai-nāđu, Kōyinūr-nāđu, Kōvūr-nāđu, Tāyanūr-nāđu and Paṛṛa-nāđu, a Nuṛamban who entered in the former's service as a Tāṇākip-pillai (commandar of army) captured his country by some vile means. When Arimittttaiya-Māvali-Vāṇarāyar dies in a war, one Śankarakutṭiyār gave asylum to his wives who were pregnant then and after a male child was born to one of them Śankarakutṭiyār led his forces into Tagadūr and captured the lost country after driving away the forces of Nuṛamban. In this attack one Nāgandai Chirukutṭiyār lost his life and in his memory the kalnāđu (hero-stone) was put up there.

cells.king: Parakēsarivarman alias Uđaiyār Śrī Rājēndra-Chōladēva, 'who took Pūravadēśam, Gangai and Kiđāram' (Rājēndra I)
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xli||456" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XLI, No. 456</button>
cells.remarks: The first inscription registers that Karkakađaivaiyriyanān alias Viyalān Marapađai-Kaṇdaṇ alias Rājēndrachōla- Viriyūr nādudaiyāṇ alias Uttamalaiyudaiya-nādālvāṇ caused the renovation of the temple of god Tīrttamalaiyudaiya-Māhādēva in Puramalai-nādu in Tagadūr-nādu, a s.d. of Nigariliśōlā-maṇḍalam. He also added a mukha-maṇdapa to the temple. Besides the chief endowed two lamps for the god Mahādēva and also the villages Kurumudali, Avvaḍi-maṇgalam and Alaiyūr in Alaimalai-nādu as tirumaḍaippallippa. The second inscription, dated in the same regnal year of king, registers that the shrines of Kshētrapāla and Chandēśvara were constructed in the temple of Tīrttamalai-Mahādēvar, by a certain Mummuḍi-chchōlā-nādu, son of Vayi-irranangaṇ and a seryant of Uttamachōlāpuramalai-nādavāṇ. Mentions Rājēndra-nādi.

cells.findspot: Chandrachūdēśvara temple
cells.date: r.y. 3, Vibhava, Tulā 15, Paurnami, Friday, Aśvati, Ś. 1218 = A.D. 1298
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 127 poṇ of gold, derived from several āyams by the king to the god Udaiyār Ševiđ-Nāyaṇār, for the tiruppani services. The gift amount (i.e. 127) included i) 40 poṇ accrued from the dēvadāna villages of the temple of god Udaiyār Ševiđa-Nāyaṇār, and the tāṇanttār, jīyara, vīravaṇukka chōlār of the temple; ii) seven poṇ of gold derived from the category which included Irāyása-nivandikēļyi-nivandam and iii) 80 poṇ collected by the Vīrachōlavaṇukkar from the village Ševiđapādi. The transaction came into force from the date given above.

cells.king: Śrī Mahāmaṇdalēśvaraṇ Tribhuvaṇamallaṇ Pūrvādhirājar alias Tāmattālvār
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a portion of land in Mēlaittūmbāđi to the east of the tank Ševidai-samudram by the above chief. It is stated that the whole land was measuring rod, 400 kuli of it being allotted to god Ševidai-Nāyaṇār, the remaining piece of land was divided into three shares of which two shares in the northern side were given to the god udaiyār Tiruvēgambamuđai in the village Kaṇđarsūriyanallūr situated to the south of the tank, and one share was endowed to brāhmanas. It is also stated that the tank Ševidaisamudaram was constructed by Kārikilān Kammānđai of Veṇpuriyāru in Āmūr-kōṭtam, a district of Jayaṅgonđa-chōla-manđalam in Mudukiraiyan-palli in Māsandi-nāđu in Nigariliśōla-manđalam.

cells.language: Sanskrit and Tamil; Grantha and Tamil, 34 lines
cells.date: r.y. : (First half of the eighth century A.D.)
cells.reference: EI, vi, no. 8, 49-53 and Plate; TPC (Tamil), 89-106;
cells.remarks: The Sanskrit portion of the grant gives the following genealogy: Vishnu; his son Aṅgiras; his son Brihaspati; his son Samyu; his son Bhāradvāja; his son Droṇa; his son Aśavatthāman. Aśvatthāman had by a Nāga woman, a son named Skandaśishya and in his family was born Skandaśishya of the present grant. The Tamil portion states that the king, at the request of Mahāvali-Vāṇarājar, issued a written order, through the executor (āṇatti), Māhēśvara-bhaṭtar, to the assemblies of kōttam and nāđu respectively of Pađuvūr-kōṭtam and Mēl-Adaiyāru-nāđu, granting the village Śārukūr, in Mēl-Adaiyāru-nāđu, a s.d. of Pađuvūr-kōṭtam to a brāhmana called Mādhavaśarma-bhaṭtar of the Vatsa-gōtra and Pravachana sūtra. The granted village was renamed as Skandaśishyamaṅgalam after the king and had the following villages as its boundaries; Manittidal on the east, Kuṛumađi on the south, Ilattai-ppāđi on the west and Kuṛukkuđi lying on the west of the Tiruvēlālamuđi on the north. The gift-village was exempted from all kinds of tax burdens including taṛi-kūlam. taṭṭārk-kāṇam, tarikkuṛai, nallā, nallerudu, ilappūtch, idappūtchi, and ullirukkai. Note: 1. These plates, three in number are of dimensions about 81/4 by 31/4". The seal is circular, 2" in diameter; it has, in relief, a kneeling bull facing to the proper left and some small emblems and a line of illegible writing round it.

cells.king: Rājakēsarivarman alias Udaiyār Śrī Rājēndra-Chōładēva (Kulōttunga I)
cells.remarks: The first fragment begins with the words Bhūmiyumtiruvam-tāmēpuṇara and mentions the name of the king. The second one records an undertaking given by the śivabrāh moṇa of the tiruṇṇāligai to provide sacred offerings to the god, having received some gold from a certain Chōla-Pallavaraiyar. The third fragment refers to the abhishēka with ghee on the day in the month of Mārgaļi with the nakshatra Tiruvādirai (Ardra) The fourth, fifth and sixth fragments seem to refer some śandi lamps.

cells.date: Ś. 1201, Bahudhānya, Magha, Pūrvapaksha, ēkādasi, Rōhiṇi = A.D. 1279
cells.remarks: Seems to record the gift of a village called Kallukkimuṭtal alias Kākkunayākanallūr in Puttūr-parṛu, by the chief Bhūmināyakar, as dēvadāna to the god Uḍaiyār Tiruvēgamba-muḍaiya-Nāyaṇār. The gift was made to provide for the sacred offerings on the days with Mūlā nakshatra, the natal star of the chief and also for making daily a garland (tirumālai) for the god. The village was given as tax-free with all its revenue from Hallenudu, narpaśu, narkidā, pañju, nūl, taṇittaniyaṇ, ellu, iruppu, kaṭti, asuvam, veṭti, payarṇ-kāṇam, vichchu-pāṭtam, amsaich-chārigai, Kudiraich-chārigai, kaṇnāla-tāyam, taṭtār-pāṭtam, etc. The gift was entrusted with four persons in the temple viz., Alaitta-lūma-bhatṭaṇ, a dēvakanmi, tavarāśappi-dāraṇ, a piḍārāṇdār and Gaṅgaikonḍa-śōla-kālār, the two persons being the kālāṇḍara of the temple, with hereditary rights to supervise its execution.
